title: A Garden Contemplation Suits
description: A Garden Contemplation Suits in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 95, “The garden”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A Gar-den con-tem-pla-tion suits, And may in-struc-tion yield, Sweet-er than all the flow'rs and fruits With which the spot is filled.

lines: Sweeter than all the flow'rs and fruits
With which the spot is filled.
But sin o'erwhelmed him with disgrace,
Oft as the garden-walk we tread,
The trespass of our legal head
Oppressed with woe, to set us free
How stupid we, who can forget,
His church as a fair garden stands,
Each tree is planted by his hand,
For grace has sown its seeds;
Where once, by nature, nothing grew
Such themes to those who Jesus love,
And make a barren desert prove

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
